newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First MPs silent on Morgan before caucus.
newsitem.headline: NZ First MPs silent on Morgan before caucus.

text.p: New Zealand First MPs went into their regular caucus meeting on Tuesday refusing to comment on the behaviour or future of MP Tukoroirangi Morgan.
Morgan has put his fate in leader Winston Peters' hands after admitting asking television stations to pay for an interview, and misleading his leader over the matter.
Heading into the 10 a.m. meeting Morgan waved and smiled at journalists who were kept away from the corridor outside the caucus room.
Peters, the Deputy Prime Minister and Treasurer in the centre-right coalition government, ran the gauntlet of waiting journalists but said nothing.

Deputy NZ First leader and Morgan's brother-in-law, Tau Henare, arrived late for the meeting after joining other, mainly Maori, MPs in talks over a Maori occupation of a picnic site near Waiouru in the centre of the North Island.
Asked if he still supported Morgan, Henare said, "I certainly do."
It was the first public comment Henare had made about the affair.
As well as discussing Morgan's future, the caucus was expected to be briefed on final details of the Budget due on June 26.
The meeting is due to finish before parliament resumes its sitting at 2.00 p.m. (0200 GMT).
